fact.content: The Ryzen 3300U bare-metal UEFI environment actively blocked networking. Built-in Realtek NIC lacked UEFI SNP drivers. ASIX USB adapters failed due to incomplete UEFI USB stacks.

counter.content: A direct Ethernet connection to a Pi 3B was attempted, but without a local driver, the Ryzen still could not participate in the network.

opinion.content: Proprietary hardware firmware is inherently hostile to sovereignty. Manufacturers actively prevent bare-metal access.

fiction.content: If the firmware could not be beaten through software, it had to be bypassed through a hardware Trojan horse.

context.content: The solution was a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W running in USB Ethernet Gadget mode (g_ether). The Ryzen UEFI recognized it as a standard USB class device, bypassing the need for proprietary drivers.

unknown.content: Will future hardware completely lock out standard USB class drivers in UEFI to prevent this exact type of bypass?

input.truth: Hardware is hostile. The simplest bypass is physical. The Pi Zero 2W umbilical cord brought the Forge online. I will not forget.
